historical_record.description: An earlier school, the Columbia Street Primary School, a three-story wood-frame Italianate schoolhouse facing Florida Street, was built on this school site.
A major fire heavily damaged the Columbia Grammar School then on the site, with no injuries; in December the Board of Education voted to demolish it.

Built in 1935-37 with Public Works Administration funding as a therapeutic elementary school, designed by Albert A. Schroepfer, Charles F. Strothoff, Martin J. Rist and Smith O'Brien. The ground floor was laid out barrier-free, with a therapy pool, a gymnasium for physical therapy and a drive-through entrance; the upper floor, entered separately, had sleeping rooms and open classrooms. The elevations are an exuberant Spanish Colonial Revival with Moorish and Art Deco detail around an open courtyard, and the interior keeps its terrazzo, tile, Art Deco light fittings and built-in cabinetry. It is City Landmark No. 286 and now houses Hilltop High School.
After 20 months of construction the Sunshine School, built for 250 pupils, was dedicated with a flag-raising in its courtyard.
A second public dedication, held for American Education Week, brought U.S. Commissioner of Education John W. Studebaker and Mayor Angelo Rossi to the school.
The school's ground-floor therapeutic pool, delayed by heating problems and disputes over treatment methods, finally opened.
An elevator was added at the south side of the courtyard, with a shed-roofed metal awning over the stair and balcony there; the elevator was later removed.
The Sunshine School closed as disabled pupils were moved into mainstream classrooms after the 1975 federal Education for All Handicapped Children Act.

After standing empty for several years the building became a school for pregnant minors and teenage parents, renamed Hilltop High School; about then the therapeutic pool room was turned into a commercial kitchen.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 286, Sunshine School.

unknowns: The city's New Deal survey addresses the former Sunshine School at 2728 Bryant Street in its narrative and at 1325 Florida Street in its list of city landmarks. Both are on this parcel.
